remaining_high_value_families: Exact canonical generation of the minimum pair-incidence face for K=10 (11-edge graphs on 10 vertices, degree <= 6) and K=20 (22 triple points and 27 double points, degree 6), scored by evaluate_portfolio. Sampled designs on that face were strictly below the baseline, but the face was not exhausted.

A proof that any portfolio with pair incidence above the minimum loses more OFFICIAL_ANY_PRIZE outcomes than the higher-order remainder can repay. The chord bound makes the pairwise term optimal at the baseline; it does not yet cap the remainder for K=10 or K=20.

taxonomy.note: Schonheim/GKP covering numbers are a different objective (cover every t-set). AG(2,7) shortened lines were built and scored. Constant-weight minimum distance is the pairwise cap already achieved.

OFFICIAL_ANY_PRIZE is monotone submodular coverage of outcomes. Nemhauser-Wolsey-Fisher greedy is the classical 1-1/e method. The minimum-incidence face is the relevant exact subproblem, not another greedy on a surrogate.

CP-SAT in global_exact_coverage_solver is certified only for n=8,d=4,k<=3. A full MIP has C(49,6) outcome rows. Symmetry reduction to the incidence face is the feasible integer model, and it is the remaining task.

Radius-2 one-exchange inside intersection<=1 was already certified for the M3+ objective. This run adds unconstrained one-exchange on the exact any-prize objective. Late acceptance, ejection chains, and VNS do not change the face that has to be searched.
SA, ACO, ALNS, GRASP+path-relinking, and tabu already exist as classical covering heuristics. They minimize block count for C(v,k,t), which is not fixed-K any-prize. No marketing GA was prototyped.
k-DPP is already a diversity sampler in the repo, not an exact maximizer. A DPP kernel cannot beat a design that already minimizes every pairwise winning intersection.

M3+ is coverage of 6-sets by the triples inside each ticket. The any-prize rescue term is the same ground set plus a partial special. Hypergraph matching does not add a variable the incidence face misses.
McKay canonical augmentation is the right way to enumerate the minimum-incidence face without label duplicates. It was not run. B649 label symmetry makes unlabeled enumeration the remaining search.

Pairwise intersections I(t) were computed exactly for t=0..6. I(t) lies on or above the chord through I(0) and I(1), so S2 is minimized by the baseline histograms. K5 remainder above that floor is 0. K10/K20 remainders are positive and not yet capped.

Numpy bitwise_count over the full main-draw mask array scores a K20 portfolio in well under a second. Roaring bitmaps do not shrink a dense 14e6-bit draw space enough to change which neighborhood is reachable.
SIMD popcount is already what numpy.bitwise_count uses. A GPU port would multiply evaluations, but the open problem is the unlabeled minimum-incidence face, not raw portfolio throughput.

Official result downloads and data.gov.tw dataset 72921 publish draw numbers and prize pools, not machine identity, ball-set identity, or pre-draw measurements. A 2018 open-data request for those fields was refused as outside the prize dataset.
OUT_OF_PRIMARY_SCOPE. Popular-number avoidance, payout sharing, expected payout, purchase timing, and jackpot size do not change the fixed-K any-prize event under a fair draw.

families.evidence: greedy_min_overlap_constructor and greedy_minmax_then_sum_overlap. Superseded by HARD_DIV on the same surrogate. The minimum pair incidence is now achieved, so a further overlap greedy cannot raise S2.
Radius-1 and radius-2 inside intersection<=1 are certified for M3+ and the portfolios realize minimum pair incidence. The any-prize objective on that same face was only sampled here, not exhausted.

reference_e and hard_div radius-2 exhaust one-exchange for M3+ inside the pairwise cap. Unconstrained any-prize one-exchange was sampled; the single deterministic K10 exchange did not improve. The minimum-incidence face still has multi-edge trades.
bounded_coverage_optimizer is multi-start but refuses real B649 scale. The K10/K20 configuration samples here are multi-start on the minimum-incidence face only.
covering_design_tabu7 minimizes classical C(v,k,t) block count. fixed_k_bridge explicitly does not claim a fixed-K optimum.
covering_design_setcover_sa is a classical set-cover heuristic, not fixed-K any-prize.
covering_design_setcover_ilp guards a toy domain. Full set cover of every 3-subset is a different objective from maximum partial any-prize coverage at fixed K.
No production-scale MIP. The useful model is an integer model on the minimum-incidence face, not 13,983,816 outcome rows.
global_exact_coverage_solver certifies only n=8,d=4,k in {2,3}. OR-Tools is present and was not rerun on that toy domain.
covering_design_alns is a clean-room classical covering heuristic with no any-prize objective.
covering_design_aco is the same classical covering objective.
covering_design_grasp_pr includes path relinking for classical covering, not fixed-K any-prize.
Unseeded genetic sampling appears only in legacy auto-optimizer notes. No exact any-prize mapping was found that is stronger than the incidence face.
covering_design_lagrangian is a classical covering dual heuristic.
C(49,6,2) and C(49,6,3) minimize blocks to cover every pair or triple. Fixed K=20 cannot cover every triple. The fixed-K problem is maximum partial coverage.
covering_design_gkp_bound implements Gordon-Kuperberg-Patashnik and the Schonheim lower bound for C(v,k,t). Those bounds do not upper-bound fixed-K any-prize.
Present inside covering_design_grasp_pr for classical covering.
1-exchange and radius-2 (two 1-exchanges) are done for M3+ inside the cap. 3-exchange and hypergraph trades on the minimum-incidence face are not exhausted.
Fourier adapters and EH01-EH10 are predictive-signal tests. Uniformity and ordinal-temporal batteries were null. They do not change a fair-draw union probability.
Equal-weight consensus and rank tie-breaks change which tickets are bought but were measured below a low-overlap portfolio. They are not a geometry improvement over minimum incidence.

families.family: prediction ensembles / Hedge / Fixed-Share / DMA / regime weighting
families.evidence: Hedge/Fixed-Share/regime weighting were closed after uniformity, CUSUM, and transfer-entropy batteries returned null. No expert gap remains for a regret bound to exploit.

methods.source: Exact two-ticket enumeration in this module; convexity of C(r,2) is the standard quadratic-mean argument.
methods.why: Proves the baseline histograms minimize the pairwise inclusion-exclusion term. Implemented as s2_lower_bound, not as another portfolio.

methods.source: Configuration model on the unique minimum of sum C(r,2). Not a named external repository.
methods.why: Any improvement must lie on this face or beat the chord penalty. Sampled points did not.

methods.source: Affine plane of order 7. Standard finite-geometry construction; lines shortened from 7 to 6.
methods.why: A structured design outside the minimum-incidence face. It tests whether geometry can repay extra intersections.

methods.source: Same neighborhood shape as hard_div_exact_radius_two, without the intersection<=1 filter and with the any-prize objective.
methods.why: Radius-2 search discarded these endpoints before any-prize scoring.

methods.source: Packing of disjoint 6-subsets. Already the K5 HARD_DIV portfolio up to labeling.
methods.why: Confirms K5 ties the locked fraction and meets the Bonferroni floor.

methods.source: Nemhauser, Wolsey, Fisher, Mathematical Programming 14 (1978) 265-294. doi:10.1007/BF01588971
methods.why: Greedy marginal coverage is the right algorithm when the ground set is unstructured. Here the optimum of the pairwise term is already known, so greedy would rediscover a minimum-incidence design.
Their auxiliary objective reweights multiple coverage. The canonical any-prize count is already the coverage objective, including partial specials.

methods.source: Kulesza and Taskar, Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 5 (2012) 123-286. doi:10.1561/2200000044. Repo: research/k_dpp_ticket_portfolio.py in the oos tree.
methods.why: A sampler, not an exact maximizer. Minimum incidence dominates a diversity surrogate.

methods.source: Burke and Bykov, European Journal of Operational Research 258 (2017) 70-78. doi:10.1016/j.ejor.2016.07.012
methods.why: Acceptance rule only. It does not define a neighborhood stronger than the incidence face.

methods.source: McKay, Journal of Algorithms 26 (1998) 306-324. doi:10.1006/jagm.1997.0898. Code: nauty/geng.
methods.why: The highest-value next search. Not prototyped in this pass because the face enumeration is larger than the sample budget.

pre_draw_signal: None found. data.gov.tw dataset 72921 and https://www.taiwanlottery.com/lotto/history/result_download publish numbers, sales, and prize pools. They do not publish draw-machine identity, ball-set identity, or pre-draw measurements. The 2018 open-data request for ball-set id, machine id, and ball weight was answered as outside that dataset (inspection is a pre-draw procedure, not a published series). No timestamped public series meets the causal bar.

next_tasks: Enumerate unlabeled minimum pair-incidence designs for K=10 and K=20 and score each class with evaluate_portfolio.
Prove or refute that every portfolio above the minimum pair incidence loses at least as many outcomes as its higher-order remainder can add, using the exact I(t) table.
If the face enumeration finds a strict improvement, record the isomorphism type (which triples share a point versus which triples are edge-triangles) and turn that into the next neighborhood.
